The articulation information in Assist.org not only shows a link to the admission requirements (aka our Major Specific Criteria webpage) but also Cal State LA graduation requirements that may be completed at the lower-division level, prior to transferring to the University. The diversity requirement is a graduation requirement, not an admission requirement. The diversity requirement may be completed prior to, or after, transferring to the University.


For the Cal State LA degree, students will be required to complete two courses (six units) certified as diversity courses, at least one focusing on issues of race and ethnicity and their intersectionality with other social categories that structure inequality in society. These courses can be completed either at the lower-division or upper-division level from among courses satisfying GE requirements.


Please view the General Education agreements on Assist.org for the lower-division courses that will meet the Diversity (d) and Race & Ethnicity (re) Requirements.

Students are advised to seek advisement from a counselor when planning to transfer to CSU Los Angeles and refer to the University Catalog to learn more about this major and its features. Additional admissions criteria for the major can be found on the Major Specific Criteria campus website. Please note that admissions requirements can vary by term so check back to see if there are any changes.

The Department of Asian and Asian American Studies offers an interdisciplinary B.A. degree program that examines Asian and Asian American communities within the context of history, culture, politics, racial formation, and social justice. Students learn how to analyze the intersections of race and ethnicity, gender, class, and power within local, national, and global contexts. The program emphasizes critical inquiry, analysis, and action so students can create positive change in themselves and the world around them.


Students with a degree in Asian and Asian American Studies are equipped with important skills necessary in every career, such as critical thinking, data analysis, creative problem-solving, community building, and communication. Our graduates pursue careers in education, public health, social work, counseling, journalism, public policy, international relations, non-profit organizations, community organizing, and other socially-engaged pathways.

﻿

The Bachelor of Arts degree in Asian and Asian American Studies requires a total of 120 units, of which 39 units are in the major.



*Note: Asian and Asian American Studies Directed Electives - Students must select 5 courses from the list of electives (at least 3 of the courses must be upper-division).
